questions.question: Piece of land surrounded by water on 3 sides is known as ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Piece of land surrounded by water on 3 sides is known as **Peninsula.**__
 
• A strait is a narrow passage connecting two large water bodies.
 
• A Lagoon is a Part of sea partially cut off from it by deposits of sand or coral reefs.
 
• A bay is a coastal water body that connects to a larger main body of water.

questions.question: Which of the following is a block mountain?
questions.solution:
• **Satpura mountain range** is an example of block mountain.
 
• When the earth’s crust cracks due to tension or compression, faulting takes place and block mountains forms.
 
• There are four types of mountains they are Block Mountains, Residual Mountains, Accumulated Mountains, and Fold Mountains.
 
• The** Aravalli Range** is considered to be the **oldest fold mountain system** in the world. Presently is considered a residual mountain.
 
• The **Himalayas** are **young fold mountains.**

questions.question: Digestion of food begins in which part of the alimentary canal in human beings?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Digestion of food begins in **Mouth**__.
 
• Saliva produced in salivary glands gets mixed in the mouth.
 
• Saliva contains an enzyme called **amylase **which breaks down starches into sugars.
 
• Digestion process involves **ingestion, digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion.**

questions.question: Which act allowed the British government to suppress political activities and detain political prisoners without trial for 2 years?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**Rowlatt act**__.

__
 
• The **Rowlatt Act**__ (**1919**) repressed political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years.
 
• It was legislation passed by the Imperial Legislative Council of British India.
 
• However, it received a lot of resentment from the Indian public.
 
• The non-official Indian members voted against the act.
 
• It led to the Non-cooperation movement. 

**Extra fact:**

 
• **​Vernacular Press Act:**

 
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was introduced by Lord Lytton (1876-1880).
 
• It was enacted to curtail the freedom of the Indian press.
 
• After this, the government kept regular track of the vernacular newspapers.

questions.question: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) protects farmers against which of the following?

options.text: Loss of crops due to unexplained diseases or insect infections
The high rate of interest by local currency lenders
Very dry, flood or any other natural disaster
An extreme drop in price during bumper production

questions.solution:
Option** 4** is correct, i.e. __**Extreme drop in price during bumper production**__**.**

__
 
• The **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** protects farmers against **an extreme drop in price during
 bumper production**__.

 
• MSP is the rate at which the government buys grain from farmers.
 
• Minimum Support Price is an important part of India’s agricultural price policy.
 
• It helps to incentivize the framers and thus ensures adequate food grains production in the country.
 
• Based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), the Department of Agriculture and Co-operation, Government of India, declares **Minimum Support Price** **(MSP)** for 22 crops before the sowing season.
